item.text:
Refactored the engine/view boundary to an observer model.

`Simulator` no longer constructs or calls `SimulatorView` and `GraphView` directly. It now owns a list of `SimulationObserver`s and publishes a `SimulationSnapshot` on reset and each step; viability is computed internally with `FieldStats` instead of asking a view whether the simulation should continue. The core changes are in [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/Simulator.java:7), with the new observer types in [SimulationObserver.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/SimulationObserver.java:1) and [SimulationSnapshot.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/SimulationSnapshot.java:1).

Both Swing views now implement the same observer interface and render from snapshots instead of bespoke `showStatus` calls: [SimulatorView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/SimulatorView.java:5) and [GraphView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/GraphView.java:12). I also removed the remaining graph-specific coupling from [FieldPopulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/FieldPopulator.java:6), so population seeding no longer knows about GUI color registration. `Main` is now the composition root that wires the engine to whichever observers you want: [Main.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R001_module_java/Main.java:2).

Verified with `javac *.java`. I did not run the Swing UI interactively here.
